One of them that is very popular and I know is java (swing). I've heard C# mono but not knowing the current status in other platform other than Microsoft. Any good information about the present cross-platform GUI programming language?
[LANG] In the present, which language that is cross-platform and have GUI?

Well, define cross-platform. Java and C# are bytecode languages which allows them to ignore the differences between processors (you don't have to recompile for each processor architecture (32-bit Intel, 64-bit Intel, ARM) you want to support). Java is also somewhat independent of operating systems due to not relying much on it. C# is still pretty tied to the Windows platform if you use WinForms or WPF GUI toolkits. There's a GTK# GUI toolkit, which is what Mono uses, which makes it more independent. But I would expect (without much experience to back it up) that C# is much better supported on Windows than on Linux.

Aside from the bytecode languages there are also interpreted (not compiled so run anywhere) languages like Python and Ruby. Python has a lot of cross-platform GUI toolkits like Qt, WxWidgets and GTK. Ruby I guess pretty much the same.

Even C and C++ are somewhat cross-platform in that you can use them on Windows, Linux and Mac. However with those languages you have to compile separately for each OS and processor architecture. Without some kind of compatibility layer you'll also need to write a lot of wrappers to adapt to each OS. For example Qt has a compatibility layer built-in, though of course it only goes so far.

One thing to be aware of with Java is that there are actually multiple Java implementations which aren't always perfectly compatible and Linux distros tend to not install the official Oracle one. This sometimes leads to code not performing well on Linux.

Honestly I don't like java because I've experienced many problems, so similar with C# (I know, java starts first) but currently under shadowed by C#. I'm afraid what you predict about mono support for C# is true that I'm looking for alternative.

What I mean by cross platform is that the application can run in GUI in any platform, compiled (if) in any platform without changing source code at all. Of course driver and third party component support isn't included. The GUI functionality is basic, mouse, keyboard, textbox, grid table, file access. That's it.

Realistically each platform has it's own preferred languages and each language has its preferred platform. Windows has C#/F#/VB.NET (.NET languages). Linux is more Python, Ruby, Javascript (and lots of others). Mac has Objective-C and Swift. C and C++ are shared by all but compatibility can be a bit of an issue.

Python or C++ may be your best bet. They're big enough that they're supported on all platforms. Because you can't rely on Python being installed on Windows you'll need a tool like py2exe to effectively compile it. C++ has the benefit of good tooling and once you've compiled it works just like a native app. However you may end up cross-compiling (running a compiler on a different platform than you're compiling for) and that could be tricky.
Thanks, looks like Python or C++ is a good choice for cross-platform here. As long as the source code isn't changed then it should be fine.
